top_problem: The pieces measure perfectly, but the tabla does not balance: El Barril leaves 84 pt (about 30 mm) of dead cream under four one-line beers, while El Cantarito is packed full. Each card is a landscape box with a list tacked on, not a lotería card. The boldest idea missing is a true tabla: equal portrait cards, with the figure and number filling the card, the name on the classic foot band, and the drinks on its back or beside it on a shared baseline grid.
fixes: Rebalance the deck so no card has more than 12 pt of empty space below its list: move the four beers into the lower row next to the spirits, or size row heights to the content so El Barril and La Botella close up (this fails the render's own no_card_more_than_12pt_empty check).

Put both columns on one shared row grid so item rows in paired cards line up across the gutter (for example a fixed 30 pt item module, with the cocktail serve cue joining the description line box), not just the first row of each card.

Make the subhead level one style everywhere: either add the English gloss after the middle dot on every card (CERVEZA Y SIDRA · BEER & CIDER, AGAVE Y BRANDY · SPIRITS, TINTOS... · WINE) or drop it from Clásicos and De la Casa.

Give the wine card labelled glass/bottle price columns (or a stated 'by the glass' label under the subhead), and give the spirits a one-line age/type description so all four cards share one item anatomy.

Leave at least 6 pt between the longest description line and the price column (Margarita currently has 1.9 pt) by capping the description measure at about 210 pt, and fix the baseline_anchor note (138 vs deck top 150) so the documented grid matches what is drawn.

top_problem: The headers repeat themselves instead of forming a hierarchy. Each card says the same thing three times (EL BARRIL / Beer & Cider / CERVEZA & SIDRA; LA ROSA / Wine / TINTOS, BLANCOS Y ESPUMOSO; LA BOTELLA / Spirits / AGAVE & BRANDY). The card header is 12 pt caps in a band off to the right at x=162/441 pt, only 1.5 pt larger than the 10.5 pt item names and out of line with the list edge at x=49.5/328.5 pt. The 7 pt subheads switch language from card to card: bilingual on cocktails, Spanish only on beer and wine, English on spirits. The masthead location line is also tagged as a subheader, but it uses a different style (DM Sans 500, 8.5 pt, muted, wide tracking), which gives the subheader level two styles. The measured checks pass: all margins are 36 pt; subheads sit 12 pt below the previous block and 6 pt above the first item, and 6.75 pt from subhead box to item box on every card; name-band headers sit at y=232.5/598.5 pt, 4.5 pt into bands at y=228/594 pt; all text contrast is 4.5:1 or better. The boldest idea still missing: let each lotería card name (big, in the traditional lotería lettering, in the band across the card foot) be the only section header, and drop the redundant subhead so the tabla reads as one deck.
fixes: Delete the one-subhead-per-card subheads on El Barril, La Botella and La Rosa (they repeat the card name), and keep subheads only where a card really splits into groups, such as CLÁSICOS / DE LA CASA.

Make the card name band the clear top level: at least 16-18 pt caps, set full width across the face or aligned to the list edge at 49.5/328.5 pt, so the hierarchy runs header, then subhead, then item, and each step is at least 1.4x the next.

Give every subhead one pattern, Spanish first with the English gloss after a middle dot (for example CERVEZA · BEER & CIDER, AGAVE Y BRANDY · SPIRITS, VINOS · TINTO, BLANCO Y ESPUMOSO), and raise it from 7 pt to 7.5-8 pt.
Re-tag the masthead 'IOWA CITY, IOWA' as a tagline/location element, not a subheader, so the subheader level has one style only.

Fill or rebalance the 84 pt empty space under El Barril and the 36 pt under La Botella (for example by moving the second cocktail subsection or adding the spirit descriptions) so the space below each header block is the same on every card.

lens: palette, contrast, price and number styling

top_problem: The Lotería tabla is a real, ownable idea, but the colour and number system is only half built: marigold (2.08:1) is decorative only and never carries information, La Botella drops to black so its prices look the same as its item names, and the 16 pt italic card numbers (44, 9, 8, 41) are louder than the prices, so the eye lands on the tabla numbers before the prices. The biggest idea still missing: make the Lotería palette the price system itself, so each card's colour runs through a matched price and number treatment and the prices read as part of the game.
fixes: Give La Botella a real card colour (marigold deepened to about #9A6A00 or a mezcal smoke tone at 4.5:1 or more) in place of flat black, so its prices, rule and band match the other three cards and the tabla reads as four colours.

Make the prices clearly different from the item names on every card: keep them in the card colour and add one consistent device (a small tabla-style frame or a thin marigold underline) so they stand out without being enlarged.
Shrink the Don Clemente card numbers to about 11 to 12 pt or put them in the card colour inside a small corner box, so they read as game ornament and not as a louder number than the prices.

Fill the 84 pt empty areas in El Barril and La Botella (ABV or style under each beer, pour size such as 2 oz under each spirit, set in muted small caps) so the price column has matching visual weight across the cards.
Tone down the rosa magenta (#C2185B is 4.66:1 on the featured tint) toward a deeper rosa mexicano such as #B0154F so it sits with the terracotta and agave instead of pulling against them.

lens: design concept and elevating elements vs the best bar menus in the country
top_problem: The lotería tabla is the right idea, but it stops at four framed boxes with a clip-art figure and a list. The cards don't read as real lotería cards: there is no full-bleed card face, no number-and-name cartouche, no printed-card texture, and the papel picado and generic 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' masthead are stock festive trim. Measured: margins are 36/36/36/36 pt; item left edges and price right edges each land on one value per column (49.5/283.5 pt and 328.5/562.5 pt); item gaps are 6 pt; subhead spacing is 12 above and 6 below on every card; all contrast is at least 4.5:1. But El Barril leaves 84 pt (about 30 mm) empty and La Botella 36 pt, so the tabla is visibly underfilled. The single boldest idea missing: make the whole page a playable lotería tabla, with each drink as its own mini-card (number, figure, name) on one shared card grid, and a frijol-marker or 'Lotería!' call-to-order device, so the menu is the game.
fixes: Fill or remove El Barril's 84 pt void and La Botella's 36 pt void: re-balance the tabla so both cards in each row end at their content, for example spirits and wine stacked in the right column under beer, or a shorter top row, rather than shipping empty boxes.

Push the lotería concept to the page level: draw each card as an actual printed lotería card, with a full-height illustrated face, the number in its traditional top-left box, and the name set in the card's bottom cartouche, plus a subtle printed-paper or halftone texture. At the moment each face is a small icon beside a band.

Replace the generic 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' wordmark and the edge-to-edge papel picado strip with an ownable masthead, for example a tabla header ('Lotería de la Cantina · Iowa City') with a hand-cut or woodtype-inspired title, and use papel picado once, sparingly, instead of as the default opener.

Give El Cantarito more hero weight, since it holds the best sellers and highest margins: larger item names or a signature-drink callout on the Margarita. The beer/wine one-liners ('Dry red wine.') and the description-less spirits make the lower cards read as a list, so pair each with a figure-level element such as a pour or size note, or a small tier icon, so they carry equal craft.

Make the card numerals and verses part of the system rather than footnotes: set the numbers larger in a boxed lotería style and tie the verse column's colour and weight to each card's hue, so the four cards read as one designed deck and not four framed text boxes.

measurements.grid: every card top, name band, subhead and item row sits on the 6 pt steps (offset 0.0), pass
measurements.empty_space_visual: El Barril is about 40% empty below Dry Cider and La Botella is about 35% empty below Cognac VSOP, in both print and phone
measurements.contrast_min: 5.08 (terracotta price on featured tint); every text pair is 4.5:1 or higher, pass

top_problem: The phone is a faithful stack of the print cards, so it carries print's biggest flaw: thin cards. La Botella has 3 name-only lines and El Barril and La Rosa have one-phrase descriptions, which leaves big dead areas in print and makes each phone card mostly face and little menu. The boldest missing idea: the lotería is only a label on each card. It never becomes a game the guest plays (for example a tabla grid of drinks, or frijol markers for house picks), so the phone scroll feels like four sections, not one lotería.
fixes: Fill or shrink the dead areas in El Barril (84 pt empty) and La Botella: add verified style, ABV and origin lines to the beers and a serve or age line to the spirits, or rebalance the rows so no card has more than 1 line of empty space in print or on the phone.

On the phone, turn the 2x2 tab block (about 190 px tall above the first card) into one horizontal sticky strip of four lotería mini-cards that show each card's figure and number, so the navigation itself continues the tabla idea.

Make the phone card face a compact horizontal strip (figure at about 60% scale, with the verse and name band beside it), so the first drink shows within the first screen of each section instead of after a 340 px face.

Carry one lotería mechanic across print and phone, such as a frijol (bean) marker on each card's signature drink or a numbered tabla index in the masthead, so the concept drives how people choose and is more than decoration.

Keep the price colour system but give the ink-coloured La Botella prices and band one accent (for example a marigold rule or numeral) so the lower-left card doesn't read heavier and flatter than the other three on both surfaces.

lens: Every item and price in round 12 checked against build/draft_doc.json: all 14 draft items are present (4 cocktails, 3 beers plus the cider from draft sec_cider, 3 spirits, 3 wines). Nothing is invented or dropped, every price matches (15/15/16/14, 7/8/7/8, 12/16/18, 12/11/13), and the prices are in one consistent right-aligned format with no $.
top_problem: The menu is correct but thin. 7 of 14 items print only the draft's generic line (for example 'Dry red wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.'), and the 3 spirits print no description at all. So beer has no style detail or ABV, wine has no region, and the spirits have no type or age cue. The La Botella and El Barril cards are left half empty (84 pt and 36 pt of dead space), while the cocktail card, which carries most of the value, is packed tight.
fixes: Answer the needs_input flags (beer ABV and brewery, wine region and producer, spirit brand and age) and print them. Until then, give each spirit a one-line description built only from draft facts (the draft desc 'Blanco tequila pour.' supports at least 'Tequila, blanco' and 'Cognac, VSOP'), so no item prints as a bare name.

Reorder the tabla so wine comes before spirits (Cantarito, Barril in the top row; Rosa, Botella in the lower row), matching the scorecard's order of cocktails, beer, wine, spirits. Also put the higher-margin cocktails or wine in the prime top-left and top-right spots.

Use El Barril's 84 pt of dead space as a Spanish/English beer-style note or a split between Draft and Cider, using the draft's own 'Draft' subhead. Then say so in the copy: the draft marks every beer as draft, but the proposal still asks 'draft or can'. Either print 'De barril · Draft' or explain why it's still an open question.

Label the Brut Rosé price once the glass or bottle answer comes back. The other wines are sold by the glass in the draft ('By the Glass'), so add a 'by the glass' cue under TINTOS, BLANCOS Y ESPUMOSO. Without it, the one sparkling price reads ambiguously next to the glass pours.

Make the price colour one system: La Botella's prices print black while the other three cards use their card colour. Either make all prices ink, or make La Botella's accent visibly its own, so the price style reads as one design.

top_problem: The menu is only complete for 4 of its 14 items. The four cocktails name their spirit, modifiers, glass and garnish from the draft and the recipe_versions rows. But La Botella prints Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP with no description at all: the draft's own lines ('Blanco tequila pour.', 'Añejo tequila pour.', 'VSOP Cognac pour.') were removed, so three known facts were dropped. Seven more items keep one generic line each ('Dry red wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.'), with no ABV, region, producer or pour size. The gaps are flagged in proposal.md, which keeps this out of auto-fail, but the menu is still thin, name-only in places and nowhere near publishable for a cantina whose agave list should be a centrepiece. All 14 names and prices match the draft exactly (15/15/16/14, 7/8/7/8, 12/16/18, 12/11/13), nothing is invented, and the empty Brut Rosé glass/bottle label is correctly left unprinted.
fixes: Give each La Botella item a description again from known facts, printing at least the type and age class from the draft (for example 'Blanco (unaged) tequila, 100% agave TBC' only if sourced; otherwise the draft's 'Blanco tequila pour.' wording), so no item prints name-only.

Get the missing facts listed in needs_input answered before the next round (beer ABV and brewery, wine grape region and producer, spirit brand and pour size), then print them as a consistent second line on every beer, wine and spirit.

Move the agave spirits up (for example, pair La Botella with El Cantarito in the top row, or merge tequila into a lead 'Agave' block), so a Mexican cantina leads with tequila, and fill El Barril's 84 pt of empty space with real content rather than air.

Fix the 'Hop-forward draft IPA.' description: it still says 'draft' even though the beer subhead dropped its draft claim. Confirm the format with the venue, or print the description without 'draft' until it is confirmed.

Set the La Botella prices in the card's own ink colour at the same weight as the other cards' coloured prices, or make all four cards match, and add the Brown Butter Old Fashioned dairy allergen note once the venue confirms it.

lens: flow and section order for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: The 2 + 2 tabla has no single reading order: read in rows it goes cocktails, beer, spirits, wine; read in columns it goes cocktails, spirits, beer, wine. On top of that, agave, the category that makes this a cantina, is on the weakest card (bottom-left, three bare names with no descriptions), while the beer card has 84 pt of empty space in a prime top-right spot. For this venue the order and emphasis are upside down.
problems: Section order is ambiguous in the 2x2 grid, and neither reading matches the scorecard flow (cocktails, beer, wine, spirits) or a cantina-specific agave-led flow.

The agave spirits (Blanco and Añejo Tequila) print names and prices only, in the bottom-left card. That gives the venue's signature category the least visual weight of any category. Categories are not treated equally.
El Barril (4 beers and cider) has a full-height top-row card with 84 pt of empty space. La Botella has 36 pt empty and a 49% face share. The columns are balanced by height but not by content.

Criterion 8: every beer lacks style detail beyond the draft words and has no ABV. The wines have no region. The spirits have no type or age line. All of this is flagged in needs_input rather than invented, which is correct, but the printed menu is thin across 10 of 14 items.

Criterion 3: prices share one format (whole numbers, no $) and one right edge per card. However, Brut Rosé and all beer and wine prices have no glass, bottle or pour label, and price colour changes from card to card.
No non-alcoholic section and no mezcal or Mexican lager. This is correctly asked, not added, but a cantina flow without them reads incomplete.

Prices match doc.json and the proposal source table (15/15/16/14, 7/8/7/8, 12/16/18, 12/11/13). No separate base_doc snapshot was in the round folder to diff against, so this rests on doc.json and the automatic check.
fixes: Make the reading order explicit and cantina-led: put the cocktail card first and the agave/spirits card second in the same column or row, then beer and cider, then wine, and mirror this exactly in the phone tabs.

Promote the agave card: move it into the top row in place of El Barril, and give the tequilas a flagged placeholder line (for example brand and age TBC) held in needs_input, so the card does not print as a bare price list.
Move beer and cider into the smaller lower-row card, where four one-line items fit without the 84 pt hole, and return the reclaimed height to the agave or cocktail card.

Chase the flagged facts before print (beer style and ABV, wine grape and region, tequila brand and age, Cognac house, Brut Rosé glass or bottle), and add pour or glass labels next to prices once they are supplied.
Reserve a slot at the end of the flow for the non-alcoholic / agua fresca section asked about in needs_input, so it can be added without breaking the grid.

top_problem: The copy speaks in three voices: the cocktails get rich guest copy plus serve cues, the beer and wine get terse three-word draft stubs ('Dry red wine.', 'Dry white wine.'), and the spirits card prints bare names with no description at all. The spirits also dropped the draft's own lines ('Blanco tequila pour.', 'Añejo tequila pour.', 'VSOP Cognac pour.'). So in a cantina the agave card reads emptiest, and the menu feels like one finished card next to three placeholders.
fixes: Restore a description on each spirit using only draft facts (for example 'Blanco tequila, poured neat.', built from the draft's 'Blanco tequila pour.'), rather than printing names with nothing under them; brand, age and pour size stay flagged in needs_input.

Rewrite every beer, cider and wine line in the cocktail voice, using only draft words (style plus 'draft' for the IPA, 'dry', 'sparkling', grape name), so all four cards read at the same length and warmth, and keep ABV, region and producer flagged.

Make the bilingual system consistent: every subhead should be 'Spanish · English' like CLÁSICOS · CLASSICS (CERVEZA & SIDRA · BEER & CIDER, TINTOS, BLANCOS Y ESPUMOSO · WINE, AGAVE Y BRANDY · SPIRITS), and 'Tintos' / 'Blancos' should be singular to match one red and one white.

Replace or drop the two drinking-joke verses (El Barril, La Botella) with the other traditional cantor verses for those cards, so the tone matches the Cantarito and Rosa verses and passes responsible-service standards.
Add the glass/bottle label to Brut Rosé once the venue answers, and give the masthead the venue's real name in place of the generic 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' so the copy is actually about this venue.

lens: how missing data is handled and flagged (vs build/draft_doc.json)
top_problem: Missing data is flagged carefully in doc.json meta and in proposal.md, but the printed menu does not handle the gaps. Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP print a name and price with no description line, which breaks the name/description/serve rhythm the other three cards use. Beer and wine fall back on generic filler ('Dry red wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.') with no ABV, region or pour. Brut Rosé's glass/bottle status is unknown and its price prints with no label. The flags themselves contradict each other: all three beers have subfamily 'draft', and the IPA line prints 'draft IPA', yet Pilsner and Amber Lager are flagged 'format (draft or can)' missing, while the IPA, which is also subfamily 'draft', is not flagged.
fixes: Give each spirit a one-line description built only from its own name (for example 'Unaged 100% agave' is NOT allowed without a source; use 'Blanco · neat or rocks' only if a serve row exists), and until then show the same muted placeholder line on all three so the Botella card keeps the description rhythm, with brand, age and pour listed in needs_input.

Make the beer format flags agree with the doc: either accept subfamily 'draft' as the source and remove the 'format (draft or can)' flag from Czech Pilsner and Amber Lager, or remove 'draft' from the IPA description until the venue confirms it.

Put ABV, brewery, wine region and pour size first in the needs_input questions, and have the layout reserve a slot for them (for example 'Czech Pilsner · — % · 16 oz') so they can be filled without a relayout.

Hold Brut Rosé's price as an explicitly unlabelled flag in the proposal, and ask the venue to confirm glass or bottle before print, since an unlabelled sparkling price sitting next to by-the-glass wines will be read as a glass price.

Fill the empty space in the Barril and Botella cards (the render measures up to 84 pt) with the confirmed data once it arrives rather than with decoration, and note in needs_input that there is no non-alcoholic section, since the draft has none and it is not flagged.

lens: trace printed ingredients, garnishes, glass and serve to sources
top_problem: Every printed fact traces to a source, but the copy outside the cocktails reads like placeholders from the database: 'Dry red wine.', 'Dry white wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.', and the spirits have no descriptions at all. There are no grapes, regions, ABVs or age statements, and a Mexican cantina's list has two tequilas, no mezcal and no Mexican beer, so the lotería cards are more Mexican than the drinks list.

verified.Margarita: phg.recipe_versions f06abb74-762a-4f89-81b2-76a9e4714f3c: glassware 'Rocks', method 'Shake with ice and strain over fresh ice', garnish 'Lime wheel', so 'On the rocks, lime wheel.' is sourced. Ingredient words come from menu_items.menu_description 'Tequila blanco, lime, orange liqueur, agave. Bright and citrus-forward.' 'fresh lime' and 'agave syrup' are sourced only from the proposal's cited draft-doc components ('Fresh Lime Juice', 'Agave Syrup'); recipe_components returned no rows. The print says 'blanco tequila' where the source says 'Tequila blanco'. That is acceptable English order but it is not the source spelling.
verified.Manhattan: rv 9fb77eaa-c5eb-477c-8e21-acbc89a0e942: Coupe, Cocktail cherry, which matches 'In a coupe, cocktail cherry.' The description matches menu_description 'Rye, sweet vermouth, aromatic bitters.' exactly.
verified.Brown Butter Old Fashioned: rv 7095fd3d-58fb-43f5-8e8f-1a0afadeafa7: method 'strain over a large cube', garnish 'Orange peel', which matches. The description matches menu_description.
verified.House Daiquiri: rv 14d45e57-72fa-4d23-8274-24e5c80e4b12: Coupe, Lime coin, which matches. menu_description says 'lime' and the print says 'fresh lime'; 'fresh' is sourced only through the draft doc.
verified.Beer/Cider/Wine: Printed descriptions match phg.menu_items.menu_description word for word (Czech Pilsner, Dry-Hopped IPA, Amber Lager, Dry Cider, Malbec, Pinot Grigio, Brut Rosé). No ABV, grape, region or producer is printed, so nothing is invented, but nothing is informative either.
verified.Spirits: Names only. The menu_description rows are 'Blanco tequila pour.', 'Añejo tequila pour.' and 'VSOP Cognac pour.' Printing no description is honest but leaves criterion 8 and 12 gaps.
verified.Junmai Ginjo: It is in phg.menu_items ($12) and not printed. The omission is flagged in needs_input item 6, which is correct.
verified.Verses: All four are traditional Don Clemente lotería verses: El Cantarito 44, El Barril 9, La Botella 8, La Rosa 41. Spanish accents are correct (cántaro, albañil, quedó).

problems: Criterion 12: seven of eleven non-cocktail items print generic class wording ('Dry red wine.', 'Dry white wine.', 'Dry sparkling rosé.', 'Crisp pale lager.'), and the three spirits print no description. This is taxonomy wording that fails the guest-language bar.
Criterion 12: the Margarita is the only description with sensory language. The other three cocktails are bare ingredient lists, so the voice is inconsistent.

Criterion 13: for a Mexican cantina in Iowa City the list has no mezcal, no reposado, no Mexican lager or michelada and no agua fresca or non-alcoholic section. Two of four cocktails are a Manhattan and a Daiquiri, so the drinks themselves could belong to any bar.

Criterion 13: the subheads mix languages inconsistently. 'CLÁSICOS · CLASSICS' and 'DE LA CASA · HOUSE' are bilingual, 'CERVEZA & SIDRA' and 'TINTOS, BLANCOS Y ESPUMOSO' are Spanish only, and 'AGAVE & BRANDY' is English only. The masthead 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' is a category, not a name.
Criterion 13: 'Tintos, Blancos y Espumoso' labels one wine per category as if each were a list.
Criterion 14: wine prints one price with no glass or bottle label. The pour size is still unknown and should read explicitly, not implicitly, as a glass price.
Criterion 14: El Barril has 84 pt of dead space and La Botella 36 pt. The spirits list is three name-and-price lines with no descriptions, which reads as unfinished next to the cocktail card.
Criterion 11 (minor): 'blanco tequila' reverses the source's 'Tequila blanco'. 'fresh' on the lime rests only on draft-doc component names, not on a recipe_components row.
fixes: Replace the class-label descriptions with guest-language copy built only from verified facts, and ask the venue through needs_input for grape and region for the wines, style and ABV for the beers, and producer or age for the spirits instead of printing 'Dry red wine.'
Add a short cue for each spirit (for example 'Unaged agave, served neat' only once the venue confirms the serve), or ask for the brands, so La Botella stops reading as a blank card.
Label the wine and spirit prices (glass / 2 oz pour) as soon as the venue answers, and fill the El Barril and La Botella dead space with the requested beer ABV or style lines rather than filler.
Pick one subhead language rule and apply it to all six subheads (Spanish first · English, or Spanish only), for example 'AGAVE Y BRANDY' and 'CERVEZA Y SIDRA'.

Match the Margarita wording to the source order 'tequila blanco', and give the Manhattan, Old Fashioned and Daiquiri one sensory clause each drawn from their recipe rows, so all four cocktails share the Margarita's voice.

lens: description quality and one guest voice
top_problem: The menu reads in two voices. The four cocktails get appetising, sourced copy with their own serve lines (verified in phg.recipe_versions via menu_items 14555870 Margarita: Rocks, Lime wheel; bf732e78 Manhattan: Coupe, Cocktail cherry; 0cc4e912 Old Fashioned: Rocks, Orange peel, 'over a large cube'; 44dcba6e Daiquiri: Coupe, Lime coin). Every beer, cider and wine line is a three-word database class ('Dry red wine.', 'Dry white wine.', 'Dry sparkling cider.'), taken word for word from menu_items.menu_description. 'Dry sparkling rosé.' (32a35bd3) only restates 'Brut Rosé'. The spirits (19d79518, 124f8949, 75501d63) have no description at all. Even inside the cocktail card the voice shifts: only the Margarita opens with 'Bright and citrus-forward:'. The rest are bare ingredient lists. The Lotería verses are correct and fit a cantina, but the item copy under them does not keep up.
fixes: Ask the venue for producer, region and ABV for beer and wine, then rewrite each line in the cocktail voice (for example '[Producer], Mendoza · [tasting note]'). Until then, add a one-clause guest-language note or leave the line out; do not print class labels like 'Dry red wine.', and never print a line that only repeats the item name, as 'Dry sparkling rosé' does for Brut Rosé.

Give the cocktails one voice: either every drink gets a short flavour lead like the Margarita's, or none does. The Manhattan, Old Fashioned and Daiquiri currently read as spec cards next to a styled Margarita.

lens: venue-type fit: Mexican cantina and cocktail bar, Spanish and lotería usage including verses, census ZIP 52240

The agave spirits print as bare names with no description. The Spanish is also applied unevenly: headings are bilingual only in the cocktails section; 'AGAVE & BRANDY' and every name-band subtitle ('Cocktails', 'Beer & Cider', 'Spirits', 'Wine') are English only; the headings use '&' in one place and 'y' in another; and 'TINTOS, BLANCOS Y ESPUMOSO' uses plurals for one Malbec and one Pinot Grigio and misses that the sparkling wine is a rosé. What I verified (gateway log_id 177): the four lotería numbers and cantor verses are correct Don Clemente text (44 El Cantarito 'Tanto va el cántaro al agua, que se quiebra y te moja las enaguas.'; 9 El Barril 'Tanto bebió el albañil, que quedó como barril.'; 8 La Botella 'La herramienta del borracho.'; 41 La Rosa 'Rosita, Rosaura, ven que te quiero ahora.'), with correct accents and punctuation. Every cocktail fact traces to phg.menu_items.menu_description plus phg.recipe_versions glassware and garnish: Margarita is Rocks / Lime wheel ('Tequila blanco, lime, orange liqueur, agave. Bright and citrus-forward.'); Manhattan is Coupe / Cocktail cherry; Brown Butter Old Fashioned is Rocks / Orange peel; House Daiquiri is Coupe / Lime coin. All prices match. Census row phg_census_zcta 52240 (acs2024_5yr): median age 28.6, 29.9% aged 21-34, median household income $52,960, 26.1% of households over $100k, 47.6% with a bachelor's degree or higher, 11% Hispanic/Latino. That is a university crowd on a modest median income, so $14-16 cocktails sit at the top of the local tier and the lack of any lower-priced agave or beer anchor stands out. Description quality: the beer and wine lines are the draft's class labels ('Dry red wine.', 'Dry white wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.'). They read as taxonomy, not guest language, and they are a different voice from the cocktail lines ('Bright and citrus-forward: ...'). The masthead 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' is a generic label, not a venue name (menu_projects.name is 'Bar menu'; doc venue is null).
fixes: Use one bilingual system everywhere: Spanish heading with an English gloss on every section and name band (for example 'AGAVE Y BRANDY · Agave & Brandy', 'CERVEZA Y SIDRA · Beer & Cider', 'Cantarito · Cocktails'), with 'y' used consistently instead of '&' inside the Spanish.
Rename the wine heading so it matches the three wines listed, for example 'TINTO, BLANCO Y ROSADO ESPUMOSO' or simply 'VINOS · Wine'.

Escalate needs_input item 2 as blocking for the cantina fit: ask the venue for a Mexican lager, a mezcal, a second agave cocktail and an agua fresca or other non-alcoholic option, and ask for the venue name for the masthead.

Give the spirits a guest line from the draft's own menu_description ('Blanco tequila pour.', 'Añejo tequila pour.', 'VSOP Cognac pour.') reworded into guest voice, and ask for pour sizes so the wine and spirit prices can carry a glass or pour label.

Once producer and region come back, rewrite the beer and wine class-label lines ('Dry red wine.', 'Dry white wine.') in the same appetising voice as the cocktails, and send a note to the designer about the 84 pt gap under El Barril.

The other three cards drop to thin or empty text. The spirits print only a name and a price, so the tall right-hand price column reads like a price list. Beer and wine descriptions are 3-word category labels ('Dry red wine.', 'Dry white wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.', verbatim phg.menu_items.menu_description). No wine price carries a glass or bottle label: Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11 and Brut Rosé 13 are unlabelled, and the draft price label is empty. fixes: Print the draft's own spirit descriptions under each spirit on the phone and in print (phg.menu_items.menu_description 'Blanco tequila pour.', 'Añejo tequila pour.', 'VSOP Cognac pour.'), trimmed to guest language such as 'Poured neat', so the name and price rows are not bare and the price column does not float alone.

Get the glass or bottle answer for Malbec, Pinot Grigio and Brut Rosé from the venue (needs_input #3), then print a small 'glass' label next to each wine price; unlabelled wine prices hold criterion 14 near 70.

Ask the venue for grape, region and producer (Malbec: Mendoza? Pinot Grigio: Veneto?) and for beer ABV and brewery; 'Dry red wine.' under Malbec just restates the category (criterion 12), but nothing may be added until the venue supplies a source row.

Make the subhead parallel: 'TINTOS, BLANCOS Y ESPUMOSOS' (or singular throughout), and ask the Coordinator whether the draft can add a mezcal or Mexican beer; a Mexican cantina in Iowa City with two tequilas, no mezcal and no Mexican lager under 'Agave & Brandy' / 'Cerveza & Sidra' reads as a generic bar with lotería trim (criterion 13).

Note for the designer (layout, not text): on the phone the cocktail descriptions wrap to 2 lines and the beer, wine and spirit descriptions to 0 or 1 line, so row rhythm changes from card to card; once real descriptions exist, set every card to a 1-2 line measure so price-to-name spacing matches the cocktail card.
